name: Standard tutoring lesson
description: Review, teach, worked examples, tiered practice, quick quiz, homework and a note for parents.

sections.title: Warm-up Review
sections.description: Plan a 5-8 minute warm-up for ${STUDENT_LEVEL} students that revisits the prerequisite skills for this topic. Give the teacher 3-4 quick oral or whiteboard questions with answers, and one sentence on how to spot students who are not ready.

sections.title: Teaching the New Idea
sections.description: Write the teacher's explanation of the new idea for a ${DURATION}-minute lesson. Include: the learning intention and success criteria in student-friendly language, the key vocabulary, a step-by-step explanation with one concrete model (concrete materials, a diagram or a number line), two common misconceptions and how to address them, and timing for each part.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.description: Write 3 worked examples that increase in difficulty. Each must have a full step-by-step working that a teacher can model on the board. Every numeric answer must include a check expression.

sections.title: Tiered Practice
sections.description: Write 9 practice questions: 3 with tier "foundation", 3 with tier "core" and 3 with tier "extension". Foundation questions mirror the worked examples, core questions vary the numbers or context, extension questions require reasoning or a two-step problem. Use Australian contexts (AUD, metric units, local places). Include at least one diagram where it helps.

sections.title: 5-Minute Exit Quiz
sections.description: Write 4 short quiz questions that a student can finish in 5 minutes and that test only the learning intention of this lesson. Avoid questions that copy the worked examples.

sections.title: Homework
sections.description: Write 6 homework questions for ${STUDENT_LEVEL} students: 4 consolidation questions and 2 word problems in Australian everyday contexts. They should take about 20 minutes.

sections.title: Note for Parents
sections.description: Write a short, warm note for parents in ${PARENT_LANGUAGE} (about 120 words). Explain what the class learned today, why it matters for the student's progress in Victorian Curriculum Mathematics Level ${LEVEL}, and one simple activity parents can do at home. Do not mention any individual student.
